source_review.notes: Reviewed the original LSM-tree publisher record; current official RocksDB compaction, leveled, universal, FIFO, and subcompaction documentation; current official Cassandra compaction and UCS documentation; and the primary PVLDB compaction-design-space and Dostoevsky papers. All ten final destinations returned HTTP 200. Product behavior and policy recommendations remain scoped to the cited versions and stated workloads.

evidence: Checked inclusive file ranges, level and size notation, overlap predicate, least fixed-point closure, version-edit set difference/union, and queue arrival/service notation.
Checked write, read, and space amplification are ratios only after their logical and physical numerators/denominators are declared.
Checked level size ratio T and level count L are used as simplified asymptotic intuition rather than exact implementation guarantees.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Byte units, MiB/GiB conversions, inclusive interval endpoints, sequence numbers, wall-clock age, and event-time windows remain explicitly distinct.

evidence: Recomputed fixture leveled input 2+2+8+8=20, declared output/input 18/20=0.9, tiered input 4*2=8, and 7/8=0.875.
Recomputed a 30 MiB/s deficit for one hour as 108000 MiB or 105.46875 GiB.
Recomputed the exercise burst as (600-270)*1200=396000 MiB or 386.71875 GiB and average surplus as 30 MiB/s.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Declared output sizes are fixtures; they are not derived from record-level visibility or measured storage-engine output.

evidence: Re-derived overlap closure as monotone set expansion over a finite file set, which terminates at the least fixed point for the declared rule.
Checked dQ/dt=a-s gives growing debt when arrival exceeds service and a necessary long-run stability condition E[s]>E[a] away from finite bounds.
Checked atomic publication is represented as V'=(V-Inputs) union Outputs and does not assume individual filesystem writes are globally atomic.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Queue stability is presented as a necessary capacity condition, not a sufficient latency, burst, disk-space, or stochastic guarantee.

evidence: Reviewed touching inclusive intervals, transitive range expansion, isolated ranges, L0 overlap, clean cuts, output key boundaries, equal user keys, and range-tombstone fragmentation.
Reviewed pinned snapshots, old and range tombstones, merge operands, TTL, late data, repair/replication, unselected older values, corrupt inputs, no-space, and clock/window mismatch.

Reviewed crashes before/after output and manifest sync, orphan outputs, pinned readers, conflicting/disjoint jobs, subcompaction boundaries, starvation, overload, stalls, cache pressure, file descriptors, and policy migration.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable model excludes records, versions, tombstones, snapshots, output generation, failures, concurrency, storage, caches, and performance.

evidence: The finite model starts from the unique oldest L0 seed, repeatedly adds every overlapping L0/L1 file, and independently compares the final closure set with the selected set.
The model verifies the leveled set f0,f1,g0,g1 and equal-size tiered set f0,f1,f2,f3 with exact input totals and ratio.
Tuple and NamedTuple checks establish the model inputs are represented by immutable tuple values for this run; exact output also checks oldest-first selection and aggregate validity.
invariant_checking.notes: Python tuple representation is only finite-model evidence and does not establish filesystem, process, or storage-engine input pinning.

evidence: Reviewed selection/level-shape proof from pinned version and transitive overlap closure through conflict reservation, output partitioning, and actual boundary validation.
Reviewed logical-equivalence proof from pre-compaction read semantics through conservative version/tombstone retention and equality of reads over pre/post version sets.
Reviewed crash-publication proof across unique outputs, durable content, one complete version edit, in-memory publication, recovery cases, and delayed reclamation.
Reviewed stability evidence from declared debt units through arrival/service measurement, throttling, fairness, failures, and rollback.
proof_review.notes: These are design-level proof obligations; no concrete engine implementation, filesystem model, replica protocol, or formal mechanization was verified.

evidence: Selection, logical equivalence, crash publication, and stability structures are separately labeled and list their assumptions.
Simplified leveling/tiering asymptotics, policy recommendations, and queue condition are marked as intuition, starting points, or necessary conditions rather than universal theorems.
The model limitations explicitly deny record-level deletion safety, production immutability, filesystem atomicity, I/O behavior, amplification proof, and deployment fitness.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Successful source retrieval, exact snippet output, and local validation are not generalized into academic review or production correctness.

evidence: The standard-library Python model passed exact fourteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
Independent arithmetic reproduced all stated fixture ratios, hourly debt growth, and burst-buffer quantities.
All ten final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local Markdown/front-matter/link/snippet checks passed before review.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production merge, SSTable builder, version/tombstone resolver, manifest crash recovery, filesystem durability, concurrency, fault injection, steady-state workload, hardware benchmark, or amplification measurement was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter separates trigger, picker, scheduler, merge kernel, installer, and reclaimer; treats complete selection and conservative entry elimination as correctness; and compares strategies through explicit trigger/layout/granularity/movement and workload assumptions.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed overlap closure, version/tombstone/TTL/repair constraints, output partitioning, sync and atomic manifest installation, reader pinning, conflict reservations, subcompaction, resource budgets, debt/backpressure, fairness, observability, crash testing, and steady-state evaluation.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review exposes the correctness kernel; the finite model makes two selection shapes inspectable; ten examples span closure, capacity, visibility, time, recovery, parallelism, and fairness; five matched exercises require calculation and evidence design.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, O'Neil, Cheng, Gawlick, Dayan, Idreos, RocksDB, Cassandra, database, storage-engine, distributed-systems, reliability, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither a production compaction picker, record merge, version/tombstone/TTL reclamation, output builder, manifest implementation, filesystem durability, concurrency controller, replica/repair protocol, steady-state capacity, amplification result, certification, nor deployment fitness.
